question: Does moving what a finding is out of the TrueHD crate change anything a command says or writes?
method: `Severity`, `Location`, `Provenance`, `RuleInfo`, the tally of a pass and the macro that writes a catalog of rules moved from `crates/oadec-truehd` to a crate of their own, `crates/oadec-diag`, which depends on nothing. The tally is generic over the rules it counts (`Tally<R: Rule>`), and the TrueHD crate names it for its own catalog under the names it had. A script outside the repository ran `oadec rules` every way it can be run with the binary of main before the change and with the change: the list, `--json`, `--markdown`, each of the rules by name as text and as JSON, and a name that is no rule; it compared stdout, stderr and exit codes byte for byte. `tools/old_new.py --decode-all` compared the two binaries over the streams of the work directory and the fixtures.

the_tests.of_the_crate: twelve unit tests, one of them on a catalog with everything wrong that a catalog can have wrong (a name used twice, a counter two rules claim, a name without a domain, a name that is not lowercase words, an error on the word of another tool alone) and the others on a catalog of three rules written for them; a documentation test writes a catalog with the macro from outside the crate
the_tests.of_the_truehd_catalog: the tests it had, and one that holds it to `oadec_diag::faults`
the_tests.the_transcripts: unchanged: the golden text of `rules` and of every report holds

each.mutation: a listing limit that caps the count as well
a payload the programme cannot take demoted to a warning
a name two rules share passing the catalog
a rule that fails a stream on the word of another tool alone passing the catalog
a run passing with a finding at the threshold it fails at

reading: Nothing. `oadec rules` is byte for byte what it was in each of 98 forms, 74 348 bytes, and over 125 streams the binary before and the binary after give the same 8 236 lines and 50 896 fields of reports and the same 103 362 691 041 bytes of deliveries.
